## Who Counts in the Unemployment Rate?

Under the Current Population Survey, a person counted as unemployed if they were not employed during the survey reference week and were available for work, except for temporary illness. They also had to have actively searched for a job during the four-week period ending with that week, or to have been temporarily laid off and expected to be recalled.

Passive-only job search does not qualify as active search. Someone waiting to start a new job generally needs to have actively searched as well. Whether a person receives unemployment insurance does not affect the classification.

The unemployment rate is calculated by dividing the number of unemployed people by the combined number of employed and unemployed people.
